title: Adaptive client-disconnect mitigation: KV-prefetch reconciliation and partial-token salvage
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: transient client disconnects (abrupt TCP close, mobile sleep, flaky proxies) lead to partially-generated outputs trapped in the serving runtime's in-memory prefetched KV state and batch pipelines. These partial generations are problematic for three reasons: 1) They consume GPU and KV cache resources for long tails, 2) Tool/function calls that happened during the partial generation may have side effects or external calls that are left ambiguous, and 3) developers see higher error rates or duplicate outputs when clients reconnect and retry.

Goal: implement a reconciler and adaptive backpressure strategy that: 1) salvages useful partial tokens for client reconnects when safe, 2) reconciles prefetched KV cache with resumed sessions without causing duplicate generation or stale cache usage, and 3) automatically deallocates abandoned resources within deterministic windows while preserving observability for incident debugging.

Proposed approach:
- Lease-based ephemeral buffers: attach a short-lived lease token (lease_ttl default 30s) to every streaming generation. If a client disconnects and reconnects with the same session token and generation_id within lease_ttl, attempt zero-loss resumption using the preserved KV snapshot and output suffixes.
- Orphan buffer and salvage policy: when lease_ttl expires, move the in-memory state to an optimized "orphan buffer" on the host for a secondary salvage window (orphan_ttl default 5m) during which we run lightweight heuristics to decide whether tokens are recoverable. If salvage succeeds, mark as reattachable and emit a reconnection hint in the logs; if not, compact and purge while recording a retention artifact for debugging.
- KV-prefetch reconciliation: maintain compacted MVCC-style metadata for prefetched KV entries per-generation (generation_id + epoch). On resume we validate epoch monotonicity and fast-path apply compatible KV deltas; incompatible deltas trigger an automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (e.g., shorter context or cold-start the KV).
- Function/tool-call atomicity: require tool integrations invoked during streaming to return an idempotency token. For existing integrations lacking this, wrap calls with a local sequencer that records a best-effort compensating action in the orphan buffer. On salvage we either replay (if idempotent) or flag the generation as non-resumable and emit a diagnostic.
- Adaptive backpressure knobs: observe queue depth, per-GPU outstanding token count, and realtime client heartbeat to tune batching window and admission control. If we detect an increased probability of disconnect (e.g., intermittent ACKs, elevated RTT variance), proactively tighten batch windows for the affected session and mark lower-priority requests for early shedding.
- Telemetry and SLOs: emit metrics for lease expirations, salvage success rate, KV reconciliation failures, tool-call non-idempotent hits, and orphan buffer size. Set alerting thresholds: salvage_success_rate < 90% over 5m OR orphan_buffer_size > 10% of host_mem triggers paging and on-call notification.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Short lease_ttl avoids long in-memory retention but increases chance of losing client-resumption capability; we choose 30s as conservative default and will tune based on observed mobile reconnect latencies.
- Moving state to an orphan buffer after lease expiry reduces hot memory pressure but complicates cross-host salvage if generation migration occurs; we keep salvage local-first and fall back to centralized short-term object store only if necessary.
- Enforcing idempotency for tool-calls increases integration work but is the only safe path to avoid external side-effect duplication; the sequencer is a stopgap for older integrations.

Acceptance criteria:
- New flow reduces long-tail GPU/KV memory retention by at least 50% for disconnect scenarios in our synthetic mobile disconnect test.
- Salvage success rate >= 90% for reconnects within lease_ttl in canary region.
- No observable duplicate external tool-call side effects in 1000 fault-injection runs.
- Metrics and dashboard added to Console; alerts configured for orphan buffer growth and reconciliation failures.

Rollout plan:
1) Landing feature-flagged implementation behind runtime-1.25 feature flag for internal Canary cluster.
2) Run synthetic load tests and chaos experiments (network partitions, TCP RST injection, mobile-simulated backgrounding).
3) Expand to a subset of low-traffic customers and internal dev orgs.
4) Gradual ramp with telemetry checks and rollback on safety signals.

Testing: unit tests for lease lifecycle, MVCC-style KV reconciliation, and sequencer failover. Integration tests with function-call mocks (idempotent and non-idempotent behaviors). End-to-end fault injection harness using testbed that simulates flaky clients.

Implementation notes: plan to implement lease metadata in the per-generation header (compact struct), orphan buffer backed by local tmpfs with compressed snapshot format, and reconciler as a background worker per-host. A follow-up will add cross-host centralized short-lived storage only if salvage success is too low.
